title: Inference capacity alignment and fiscal sprint review
topics: Security/compliance ask: audit logs, KMS, SOC2
Pilot timeline and right-sizing for Q1 budget
summary: Quarterly health-style checkin focused on aligning inference capacity to Crestline's Q1 fiscal sprint. Discussed recent usage spikes, some regional latency blips in eu-west, tradeoffs between burst-hosted versus reserved (dedicated) capacity, and an upcoming model upgrade. Action items: Redwood to share updated billing breakdown and a pilot runbook; Crestline to provide traffic patterns and decision date for reserved capacity by mid-December.
next_steps: Redwood: Send detailed cost delta table for 7B -> 13B plus quantized profiles (due 2026-12-15)
Crestline: Share month-of-November token distribution and p50/p95 latency slices (due 2026-12-13)
Schedule 60m pilot kickoff with SE-led benchmark run (target week 2026-12-20)
Agree on reserved capacity decision date (Crestline internal: 2026-12-22)
action_items: Priya Sharma - Compile cost comparison spreadsheet for hosted vs dedicated (due 2026-12-15)
Jonah Lee - Prepare pilot runbook and perf test scripts; include kv/prefix caching configs (due 2026-12-18)
Marta Ruiz - Export token distribution, peak windows, and region breakdown (due 2026-12-13)
Anika Patel - Confirm Q1 reserved capacity budget range and approval process (due 2026-12-20)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08 14:30 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Marta, Derek, Anika, Samir (Crestline)
---
[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time in the sprint week. quick agenda: usage, costs, a couple of reliability notes, and then pilot + decision timeline.
[00:16] Marta: Yeah thanks Priya. we've had a couple of high-traffic days in Nov, sorry for the late send of logs. we've seen token counts spike about 3x on 11/17 for mortgage chatbot flows.
[00:28] Derek: and the eu-west region had more timeouts than we expected, 504s at p99. not huge error rate but noticeable latency.
[00:42] Jonah: okay nod, we saw a correlated queueing effect — probably at the batching layer when many short requests arrive. could be solved by prefix caching or smaller batch windows, depends on latency SLO.
[00:56] Anika: from finance side, the November bill exceeded forecast by 27% so we need to lock a plan for Q1. reserved capacity looks attractive but we need numbers.
[01:12] Priya: totally — that's why Jonah and I prepared a preliminary delta table. rough numbers: moving to reserved for a baseline 2x instance pool reduces per-token cost by ~22% for your observed mix, but adds a monthly commit.
[01:29] Samir: can you show the breakdown for model size? we're evaluating staying on 7B or moving to 13B for better quality.
[01:39] Jonah: yes, 13B increases token costs ~1.6x in hosted, but with int8 quantization and batching improvements we estimate 1.2x on dedicated. quality bump noted on longer context tasks. caveat: kv cache and longer sequences will raise memory pressure.
[01:58] Marta: that memory thing worries me; we run per-user sessions with long contexts — the cache blow-up is real. any recommendations there?
[02:10] Jonah: two prongs: 1) prefix/KV caching to avoid re-compute for repeated prompts, 2) sequence-length caps plus summarization to bound KV size. we can show tradeoff curves in pilot.
[02:28] Derek: about the eu-west latency — we had some requests routed to us-east because policy fallback happened during an outage, which increased RTT. how do we control routing better?
[02:41] Priya: smart routing policies can pin you to region-first, with automatic fallback to nearest replica only when capacity is unavailable. we also have canary rollouts so model upgrades don't hit all regions simultaneously. maybe for you we recommend a regional primary + limited cross-region fallback.
[02:58] Marta: what's the compliance story — audit logs, KMS, any SOC2 gaps for our auditors?
[03:08] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and we provide immutable audit logs for request metadata. hosted has encrypted-at-rest and SOC2 Type II compliance; Private adds VPC peering options and HSM/KMS integration. I'll attach the security brief.
[03:25] Anika: do we get RBAC for team-level cost visibility? we need finance to see token spend per product line.
[03:33] Jonah: yes console exposes token-level breakdown and you can create API keys per product with per-key cost attribution and tags. we can demo per-key dashboards during the pilot.
[03:45] Samir: what about fallback quality — if a model variant is used in low-cost mode, how do we ensure UX doesn't degrade?
[03:54] Priya: rollout policies let you route a percentage of traffic to a cheaper variant and keep a quality cohort on the full model; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload, and we tie regressions to prompt-sets so you get alerts.
[04:09] Marta: action items for us: we need the precise cost delta to present to procurement. can you send that by next week?
[04:17] Priya: yes, we'll send the 7B vs 13B top-line and a second sheet with dedicated commit scenarios.
[04:25] Derek: pilot — we want to run a benchmark that includes our long-session churn and cache-hit scenarios. can the SE run that?
[04:33] Jonah: absolutely, we'll include KV/prefix cache scenarios plus a region-latency run.
[04:39] Anika: any procurement blockers? contracts?
[04:43] Priya: standard reserved contract language — we'll share an MSA + SOW draft. legal details can go through your procurement; we try to keep commit terms flexible.
[04:52] Marta: timeline — can you give us a recommended commit size for Q1?
[04:58] Jonah: based on Nov traffic, a conservative reserved pool sized at 60% of peak gives 95% headroom for normal variance and leaves burst hosted fallback. we'll model three scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Priya: ok to recap — Redwood sends cost delta + demo runbook by 12/15, Crestline sends token distro by 12/13, SE pilot scheduled week of 12/20. internal decision target 12/22. any objections?
[05:23] Samir: no objections, just need clarity for budget sign-off.
[05:27] Anika: will the cost spreadsheet include amortized network egress and storage?
[05:31] Priya: yes we'll include expected egress and storage delta between hosted/dedicated.
[05:36] Derek: small note — on the eu-west outages, can you run a postmortem with trace ids? we'll share logs after the call.
[05:43] Jonah: please send logs and we will correlate with routing and kernel picks; sometimes the compiled kernel path increases latency under certain sequence lengths.
[05:52] Marta: thanks. also, is SOC2 certificate current? our auditor asked for the attestation date.
[05:57] Priya: SOC2 attestation is 2026-09-30; I'll attach the cert.
[06:03] Anika: great, thanks everyone.
[06:06] Priya: thanks all, we'll follow-up with the materials and pencil in the pilot kickoff.
---
End of transcript. Notes: transcription has some garbling, proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., kernel path references, 'kv' sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee').
